title: FARSIQA: Faithful & Advanced RAG System for Islamic Question Answering
measurement_description: The paper measures the performance, answer correctness, relevance, faithfulness (groundedness), and noise robustness of FARSIQA, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system designed specifically for complex, multi-hop question answering in the Persian Islamic domain. It evaluates the model's ability to accurately answer theological and historical questions, synthesize evidence neutrally, and gracefully reject out-of-scope or unethical religious queries.
findings: The FARSIQA system, which implements a novel iterative and adaptive RAG framework (FAIR-RAG), significantly outperformed a naive RAG baseline in the Persian Islamic domain. It achieved an Answer Correctness score of 74.3% and a near-perfect Negative Rejection rate of 97.0% for out-of-scope queries. The study demonstrated that using a dynamic allocation of language models (Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.1-70B, and DeepSeek-R1) for different sub-tasks optimizes both computational cost and the faithfulness of the generated religious answers, mitigating hallucinations commonly found in generalized models.
